WRITE TASK. You own EXACTLY ONE FILE: `C:\openvela_ws\openvela\contest2026_416_dianzinongmingong\app\zhaoxi_ui\src\zhaoxi_ui.c`. Do NOT touch any other file. Do NOT build. Do NOT run git.

## Context (all verified by prior investigation)
- Board: BES2800BP, RM69330 round panel. Display reported as **464x454** by LVGL fbdev; app hardcodes `SCREEN_W 454 / SCREEN_H 454`. Keep 454x454.
- LVGL is **9.1.0**. Use v9 APIs: `lv_screen_load()`, `lv_screen_active()`, `lv_obj_create(NULL)`. `lv_scr_load` is a deprecated alias.
- `CONFIG_LV_USE_TILEVIEW=y`, `CONFIG_LV_USE_KEYBOARD=y`, `CONFIG_LV_USE_TEXTAREA=y`, `CONFIG_LV_USE_LABEL=y`, `CONFIG_LV_USE_BUTTON=y` — all available. Keyboard default size is 100%x50% (covers nav) — you must size it yourself.
- Touch works via `/dev/input0` (TMA525C), polling, reports TOUCH_DOWN/MOVE/UP. Single touch only. Gesture recognition is OFF, but tileview drag-scroll uses normal press+move, which works.
- Fonts: custom CJK subsets `zhaoxi_font_20/22/24/28` are declared via `LV_FONT_DECLARE` and used everywhere. `lv_font_montserrat_48` is used for the clock (ASCII only). **A separate agent auto-extracts all CJK chars from this file to build the fonts, so just write Chinese normally — no need to track characters.** Do not use any font other than `zhaoxi_font_20/22/24/28` and `lv_font_montserrat_48`.
- App stack size is 16384; LVGL heap is a fixed 2MB TLSF pool. Keep screen-build functions shallow.
- Data dir on the RUNNING firmware is **`/data/ai_agent`** (NOT `/data/agent`). Always try `/data/ai_agent/<file>` first, then `/data/agent/<file>` as fallback. The `/data` mount is tmpfs, so files may be absent — handle gracefully.
- The main loop is single-threaded: `while(1){ idle=lv_timer_handler(); usleep(idle?idle:1 *1000); }`. Keep that.

## Required features

### 1. Three-screen UI with BOTH swipe and nav buttons
Use ONE LVGL screen containing:
- a **tileview** (`lv_tileview_create`) sized to fill the area ABOVE the nav bar, with 3 tiles arranged horizontally (`lv_tileview_add_tile(tv, col, row, dir)`; use cols 0,1,2, row 0). Enable horizontal scroll so the user can **swipe left/right**.
- a **persistent nav bar** as a sibling below the tileview (reuse the existing 3-button design with 首页/对话/设置).
- Nav buttons must call `lv_tileview_set_tile_by_index(tv, idx, 0, LV_ANIM_ON)` (check exact signature in `C:\openvela_ws\openvela\apps\graphics\lvgl\lvgl\src\widgets\tileview\lv_tileview.h` before using) AND update the active-button highlight color.
- Add an event callback on the tileview for `LV_EVENT_VALUE_CHANGED` (tileview emits this when the active tile changes) to keep the nav highlight in sync with swipes. Verify the event name in the tileview header/source.
- Keep a global `lv_obj_t *g_tileview;` and the nav button objects array so highlight can be updated.

**Tile 0 — 首页 (home)**: the current content: status bar (WiFi + AI Ready), big clock card (`lv_font_montserrat_48`), date label, greeting label, weather card, task card. Keep the existing look (dark theme colors already defined).
**Tile 1 — 对话 (chat)**: an LVGL **textarea** + **keyboard** + a log label. Typing is LOCAL ONLY (no agent round-trip): when the user presses the keyboard's OK/ready button (LV_EVENT_READY) or a Send button, append the text to the log label with a prefix like `> ` and clear the textarea. Also log it to the console with `LV_LOG_USER("INPUTDBG: %s", text)`. Size the keyboard to about 220px tall and place it at the bottom of the tile so it does not cover the log. Show the latest REMINDER.md content on this tile too.
**Tile 2 — 设置 (settings)**: read-only info screen: WiFi/network status (from NET_STATUS file), device uptime or build info if cheap, task count, and a short note. Keep it simple.

### 2. File-driven state (poll with lv_timer, same pattern as existing task timer)
Implement a generic helper `static bool read_first_line(const char *primary, const char *fallback, char *buf, size_t buflen)` that opens the primary path, falls back to the fallback path, reads the first non-empty line, strips trailing CR/LF, and returns true on success. Paths:
- `/data/ai_agent/WEATHER.md` (fallback `/data/agent/WEATHER.md`) → weather card value. If missing/empty, display `暂无数据` in a dim color (do NOT show `-- C`).
- `/data/ai_agent/REMINDER.md` (fallback `/data/agent/REMINDER.md`) → show on tile 1 (chat) and optionally a small badge.
- `/data/ai_agent/NET_STATUS` (fallback `/data/agent/NET_STATUS`) → content is either `CONNECTED <ip>` or `DISCONNECTED`. Update the WiFi status label text and color (green when CONNECTED, orange when DISCONNECTED/absent). If the file is absent, show the last known state but do not crash.
- Existing TASKS.md counting must be preserved (`/data/ai_agent/TASKS.md` primary, `/data/agent/TASKS.md` fallback) — keep the `- [ ]` counting logic.
Poll all of these from ONE `lv_timer` at 2000ms (replacing/extending the current 5000ms task timer), calling `read_first_line` for each. Keep the clock timer at 1000ms.
IMPORTANT: guard every `lv_label_set_text` — if the label pointer is NULL (e.g. before build), skip.

### 3. Built-in self-diagnostic layer (CRITICAL — this is how we verify in ONE flash)
Add console diagnostics that can be read over the serial console:
- On startup, after building the UI, log one line: `DIAG READY weather=<ok|none> reminder=<ok|none> net=<ok|none> tasks=<n> fonts=4`
- In the file-poll timer, when a value CHANGES, log `DIAG FILE <name>=<value>` (only on change, to avoid spam).
- Add a full-screen invisible clickable object OR add a pointer event callback on the tileview/screen that logs `DIAG TOUCH x=<x> y=<y> state=<pressed|released>` on every touch event. Use an LVGL indev event or an event cb on a transparent full-size object placed on `lv_layer_sys()` (top layer) — but make sure it does NOT swallow clicks needed by buttons/keyboard. The SAFEST approach: attach `LV_EVENT_PRESSED`/`LV_EVENT_RELEASED`/`LV_EVENT_PRESSING` callbacks to the tileview and log coordinates via `lv_indev_get_point(lv_indev_active(), &p)` — verify the v9 API name in the LVGL tree first. If `lv_indev_active` is unavailable, use `lv_indev_get_act()` (v8 alias) only if it exists. Log at most once per press to avoid flooding.
- Log `DIAG NAV idx=<n>` whenever a nav button or tile change switches tiles.
- The main loop should log a heartbeat `DIAG ALIVE <n>` every ~30 seconds so we can detect a hang.

### 4. Robustness requirements
- The app currently returns early if `lv_is_initialized()` — KEEP that guard (it prevents dual-LVGL conflicts).
- Keep the existing `boardctl(BOARDIOC_INIT, 0)`, `lv_init()`, `lv_nuttx_init()` sequence and the `result.disp == NULL` check.
- Keep the dark theme setup (`lv_theme_default_init`) and `COLOR_*` macros.
- Never dereference a possibly-NULL label. Store all label pointers in globals and NULL-check before use.
- Do NOT call any socket/network API from this file. Do NOT use pthreads.
- No memory leaks on repeated tile builds (build once; do not rebuild tiles).
- Add NO comments except brief section headers in the existing style. Match the file's existing style.

## Verify before finishing
- Read `lv_tileview.h`, `lv_textarea.h`, `lv_keyboard.h`, and `lv_indev.h` in `C:\openvela_ws\openvela\apps\graphics\lvgl\lvgl\src\` to confirm EVERY API you call exists with the exact signature in LVGL 9.1. Report the exact functions you verified.
- Confirm the file compiles logically: balanced braces, all declared statics used, no undefined symbols.
- Confirm you did not exceed reasonable complexity (aim for a single coherent file, ~600-800 lines is fine).

## Report back
- The list of LVGL APIs you verified (name + header:line)
- How you implemented swipe+button sync
- The exact diagnostic strings emitted
- The file path + final line count
- Any API that did NOT exist and what you used instead

79: static int count_pending_tasks(void)
80: {

82:     if (fp == NULL) {
83:         /* Older firmware keeps agent data under /data/ai_agent */
84:         fp = fopen(TASKS_FILE_LEGACY, "r");

86:             return 0;

90:     int count = 0;
91:     char line[256];
92:     while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), fp) != NULL) {
93:         const char *p = line;
94:         while (*p == ' ' || *p == '\t') p++;
95:         if (strncmp(p, "- [ ]", 5) == 0) {
96:             count++;
97:         }
98:     }
99:     fclose(fp);
100:     return count;
101: }

The tileview's own `LV_EVENT_VALUE_CHANGED` (fired on scroll-end) also calls `nav_set_active(lv_obj_get_index(active_tile))`. `nav_set_active` updates highlight and logs only on change, so button and swipe stay in sync without duplicate logs.
